result.title: Findings-aware Language-Image Pretraining for CT Volume Interpretation
result.summary: Computed tomography (CT) provides diverse patient information and various clinical tasks, for which numerous deep learning models have been investigated. Recent years have seen the development of vision-language foundation models that can comprehensively extract clinical features, driven by representation learning that combines CT volumes with radiology reports. Existing approaches typically adopt Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP)-based representation learning, where pairs from different cases are, in principle, treated as negative pairs such that the volume and report embeddings are pushed apart. In the biomedical imaging, however, treating different cases as negative pairs is not always appropriate, particularly when clinical similarity exists. In this study, we propose a supervised representation learning framework grounded in clinical knowledge from language foundation models, rather than the weak supervision used in CLIP. Specifically, we utilized a large language model to extract abnormal finding phrases from reports. We then explicitly constructed the target features that the image encoder should output, as the semantic representation of the extracted findings using a biomedical text embedding model. Our Findings-aware Language-Image Pre-training (FiLIP) outperformed weakly supervised approaches in multi-label zero-shot finding classification in both in-domain and external-domain evaluations, and also proved effective when fine-tuned for the downstream task of radiology report generation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 FiLIP：用大语言模型从 CT 放射报告中抽取异常发现短语，再经生物医学文本嵌入模型生成显式目标特征，直接监督图像编码器，以避免 CLIP 式对比学习把临床相似病例当作负对；在多标签零样本发现分类（域内与外部域）及报告生成微调上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 以显式构造的目标表示替代弱监督对比目标，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态的监督目标设定、以及语义相近样本被误作负样本的问题提供可供核查的训练侧线索，但论文本身不研究推理过程或 latent 步骤生成。
